What if air became as thick as honey, for five seconds?
Tower Bridge, London. Rush hour.
A plane passes over every ninety seconds.
Then the air turns as thick as honey.
The rain stops dead.
You can't pull in a breath.
Sound dies within a metre.
Every bird in the sky just hangs.
Every fuel engine chokes.
But the worst is up there.
Jet engines can't swallow it.
Every jet on Earth flames out.
Ten thousand planes, all at once.
Eight billion people. No breath.
At second five, the air comes back...
and every engine must restart. At once.
In nineteen eighty-two, a jumbo jet lost all four engines.
Still want to fly home tonight?
And then the water falls back...
and a ginormous tsunami appears out of nowhere.
